title: Abelian inverse image preserves constructibility with finite geometric stalks
statement: Let $g:Y\to X$ be an arbitrary morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $E$ be an abelian sheaf on the small etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Suppose the underlying sheaf of sets of $E$ is constructible: it has a finite partition into constructible locally closed subschemes with finite locally constant restrictions, with finite geometric stalks. Then the underlying sheaf of sets of $g^{-1}E$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is constructible in this same sense. No Noetherian hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Choose a finite lisse stratification of the underlying set sheaf. Pull it back along $g$ using the scheme stratification pullback: the preimages of its constructible locally closed strata are constructible and locally closed, disjoint, and cover $Y$.

For each pulled-back stratum, the pullback composition isomorphisms and the Cartesian relation identify the restriction of set inverse image with inverse image of the original lisse restriction. Pull a trivializing etale cover back to a jointly surjective etale cover. The restriction comparison and constant-sheaf inverse-image theorem show that each member trivializes the new restriction.

For any algebraically closed geometric point upstairs, the set inverse-image stalk theorem gives a bijection with the original stalk at the composite point. Thus all new stalks on each stratum are finite. The inverse-image algebraic-structures comparison identifies the set inverse image with the underlying sheaf of the abelian inverse image. Pull that isomorphism back to the strata and transport local constancy and stalk finiteness; the pulled-back stratification witnesses the conclusion.

    (E : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (hE : IsConstructibleEtaleSheafOfSets

        (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).obj
